title: Instruction Protocols: Moral Licensing, Instrumental Apology and Insincerity Aversion
author: Elias Khalil
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tutenwn

steps.title: Conduct Part 1 of the Experiment
steps.instruction: Administer the first part of the experiment using on-screen, paper, and read-aloud instructions. Ensure participants can ask questions and are prohibited from communicating with others.

substeps.instruction: Inform participants that payment for either Part 1 or Part 2 will be decided by a coin toss, and all receive $10 for completion.
Randomly match participants and assign roles of 'proposer' and 'responder'.
Responder decides to accept (both receive the proposed split) or reject (both receive $0).

steps.title: Conduct Part 2 (Baseline Treatment)
steps.instruction: Repeat the game from Part 1 using only on-screen instructions. Participants maintain their original roles but are matched with different people.

steps.title: Conduct Part 2 (Known Apology Treatment)
steps.instruction: Repeat the game from Part 1 using only on-screen instructions with a different partner, incorporating a pre-proposal apology option.

substeps.instruction: Before making the offer, the proposer is given the choice to send the message: 'Sorry for the proposal.'
If chosen, the responder receives the message simultaneously with the proposal.

steps.title: Conduct Part 2 (Unknown Apology Treatment)
steps.instruction: Repeat the game from Part 1 using only on-screen instructions with a different partner, incorporating a post-proposal apology option.

substeps.instruction: The proposer records their proposal (which cannot be rescinded).
After recording, the proposer is given the choice to send the message: 'Sorry for the proposed offer.'
If chosen, the responder receives the message 'Sorry for the proposal' simultaneously with the proposal.

steps.title: Conduct Part 3 (Bonus Round)
steps.instruction: Administer the bonus round via on-screen instructions for all treatments.

substeps.instruction: The responder chooses an unconditional additional amount between $0 and $5 ($0, $1, $2, $3, $4, or $5) to be given to the proposer.
The proposer is informed that the responder is making this decision and will be made aware of the final amount selected.
